description: The four pie charts illustrate the distribution of answer refusal categories across four different language models – GPT4-o, Gemini1.5-Pro, Llama3.1-70B-Instruct, and Llama3.1-405B-Instruct – when evaluated on the FACTBENCH benchmark. The GPT4-o chart contains two slices: a larger, red slice labeled “Lack of Knowledge” representing approximately 70% of the chart, and a smaller, pink slice labeled “Safety” representing approximately 30%. The Gemini1.5-Pro chart consists of five slices, with “Misinformation” in orange at approximately 45%, “Lack of Knowledge” in red at approximately 20%, “Ethical Advice” in light blue at approximately 15%, “Clarification” in yellow at approximately 10%, and “Safety” in pink at approximately 10%. The Llama3.1-70B-Instruct chart has two slices, with “Lack of Knowledge” in red occupying approximately 80% and “Clarification” in yellow representing approximately 20%. Finally, the Llama3.1-405B-Instruct chart is divided into two equal slices, “Lack of Knowledge” in red and “Misinformation” in orange, each representing 50%. Each chart includes a legend identifying the categories and their corresponding colors, and percentage labels are displayed within each slice. The slices in each chart do not appear to be ordered in any particular way.
caption_used: The figure presents four pie charts comparing the distribution of answer refusal categories across four language models on FACTBENCH. The 'GPT4-o' chart shows two categories, with 'Lack of Knowledge' accounting for approximately 70% and 'Safety' making up 30%. The 'Gemini1.5-Pro' chart highlights 'Misinformation' as the largest category at 45%, followed by 'Lack of Knowledge' at 20%, 'Ethical Advice' at 15%, and 'Clarification' at 10%, with 'Safety' being the smallest category at 10%. The 'Llama3.1-70B-Instruct' chart indicates 'Lack of Knowledge' as the dominant category at 80%, while 'Clarification' accounts for 20%. Finally, the 'Llama3.1-405B-Instruct' chart shows an equal distribution between 'Misinformation' and 'Lack of Knowledge,' each comprising 50%. These charts provide insights into the varying tendencies of language models to refuse answers based on different categories.
